name: query_metrics
description:
Query an instant vector at the supplied at timestamp. Use when sample values are needed to check a hypothesis. Reuse confirmed metric names and labels; discover_metrics, if available, can find unknown names and labels. Skip queries when existing evidence already answers the question.

Returns normalized observations with evidence IDs, or an empty evidence list when no samples match. An empty result does not establish health: check names, labels and sample availability before retrying. Do not guess names or label variants.

Conditional example: ONLY if request_count_total and the label job="orders" are confirmed, the expression 'request_count_total{job="orders"}' can inspect those samples.

inputSchema.description: Query an instant vector at the application-selected end time.

expression.title: Expression
expression.description: PromQL expression returning an instant vector, using confirmed metric names and label values. Not a bare range vector or scalar.

at.title: At
at.description: Timezone-aware timestamp at which to evaluate the expression.

inputSchema.title: MetricQuery

name: discover_metrics
description:
Discover metric names and label examples in the supplied start/end window before writing PromQL. Use when relevant names or labels are unknown, including after an empty query with suspected mismatches. Reuse previously discovered metadata; skip discovery when names and labels are known or evidence is sufficient.

Returns metrics containing metric, label_keys and example_labels. Empty example_labels means no examples were included, not that the metric has no labels; pass its exact returned name as metric to inspect it. possibly_truncated, omitted_metrics and labels_truncated mark incomplete coverage. Empty discovery may mean service labels differ; bounded global discovery can reveal them. Absence never proves health. Metadata has no evidence IDs or sample values and cannot be cited.

For example, set service="orders" to find candidates for that service in the supplied window. If retained evidence already supports an explanation request, answer without another query.

inputSchema.description: Select a bounded metric-name or label catalogue.

service.title: Service
service.description: Exact service value matched against service_name, service or job labels, not a substring or regex. Omit or use null for a bounded global catalogue when these labels are unknown.

metric.title: Metric
metric.description: One exact metric name returned by discovery, not PromQL or a regex. Set it to inspect that metric's label examples; omit or use null to discover distinct metric names first.

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: Maximum distinct names and maximum series inspected per metadata request (1-50, default 20), not an evidence count or time range. Results may be incomplete even at this limit.

inputSchema.title: MetricDiscovery

name: search_traces
description: Find recent Jaeger traces for one service in the supplied start/end window.

name: get_trace_detail
description:
Inspect a known trace: return error spans plus up to 20 longest successful spans, including service, operation, duration_ms, is_error and parent_span_id when available. Use successful spans to investigate latency even when there are no errors. Parent and child durations overlap; do not sum them. Results are bounded, not a complete span tree. This tool does not filter by time.

Use the exact attributes.trace_id from trace or log evidence, not the evidence's id. If no trace ID is available, search_traces or search_logs may supply one when those tools are available. Do not invent a trace ID or reconstruct an abbreviated value.

inputSchema.description: Require an actual Jaeger trace ID rather than an evidence UUID.

trace_id.title: Trace Id
trace_id.description: Copy the exact attributes.trace_id from returned trace or log evidence: a 16 or 32 character hexadecimal Jaeger ID. Not an evidence UUID or span_id. Never invent or pad an ID.

inputSchema.title: TraceDetail

name: search_logs
description: Find OpenSearch logs for one service in the supplied start/end window, optionally matching text. Results are a bounded sample; absence of a message does not prove absence of a fault. Event time is preferred; when it is absent or zero, observation time is used, marked by timestamp_source=observedTimestamp in evidence. Observation time is not proof of the exact event occurrence time.

inputSchema.description: Select service logs with an optional body-text filter.

service.title: Service
service.description: Exact telemetry service name. Not an operation name or a list of services.

text.title: Text
text.description: Optional log-body search terms. Omit or use null to apply no body-text filter. Not a trace ID filter or a regex.

inputSchema.title: LogSearch
